lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Quote one sensory image from: "Smoke ribbons the cold alley" and name the sense.

FEEDBACK
Smoke ribbons — sight (and possibly smell if continued). Verb ribbons creates a visual shape.

CHECK
Summarising the topic without quoting imagery skips the poet’s craft.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Find six sensory images across two short poems. Sort them by sense, then write a paragraph explaining which image is strongest and why.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Imagery in poems appeals to the senses; readers quote the sensory words and explain the picture or feeling they create.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.

Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Find six sensory images across two short poems. Sort them by sense, then write a paragraph explaining which image is strongest and why. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using imagery on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Summarising the topic without quoting imagery skips the poet’s craft.. Correction: Smoke ribbons — sight (and possibly smell if continued).. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Summarising the topic without quoting imagery skips the poet’s craft. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating imagery on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with imagery, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about imagery with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for imagery. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..
